chapters.title: Chapter 1: Normal Hemostasis and Coagulation Physiology
chapters.description: Fundamental principles of primary and secondary hemostasis, the cellular and molecular components of clot formation, and normal regulation and resolution of thrombosis.
subtopics: Platelet adhesion, activation, aggregation and secretion
Coagulation cascade: intrinsic, extrinsic and common pathways
Role of thrombin, fibrinogen and fibrin formation
Natural anticoagulant systems: antithrombin, protein C/S, TFPI
Fibrinolysis and plasmin-mediated clot breakdown
Interplay between endothelium, platelets and coagulation factors
Normal laboratory markers of hemostasis (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer, platelet count)

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Platelet Biology and Platelet Receptors
chapters.description: Structure and function of platelets, key surface receptors involved in activation and immune interactions, and mechanisms of platelet clearance and production.
subtopics: Platelet structure, megakaryocyte origin and thrombopoiesis
Major platelet receptors (GPIb-IX-V, GPIIb/IIIa, FcγRIIa)
Platelet granules (alpha and dense) and released mediators
Mechanisms of platelet activation and aggregation
Platelet lifespan and mechanisms of thrombocytopenia
Platelet testing: blood film interpretation, platelet function assays
Platelet factor 4 (PF4): synthesis, storage, and physiologic roles

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Immunology Relevant to Antibody-Mediated Thrombocytopenia
chapters.description: Basic immune mechanisms underlying antibody formation, immune complex biology, and Fc receptor-mediated cellular activation relevant to immune thrombocytopenias.
subtopics: Antibody classes (IgG, IgA, IgM) and Fc-mediated effector functions
Immune complex formation and complement activation
Fcγ receptors (including FcγRIIa) structure, polymorphisms and signaling
Mechanisms of antibody-mediated platelet activation and clearance
Autoantibody vs alloantibody responses
Immunomodulation: IV immunoglobulin (IVIG) mechanisms (Fc blockade, anti-idiotype, FcRn effects)

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Heparins and Related Anticoagulants: Pharmacology and Mechanisms
chapters.description: Pharmacology, mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetics, monitoring and adverse effects of unfractionated heparin (UFH), low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWH), fondaparinux and direct anticoagulants.
subtopics: UFH: mechanism (antithrombin potentiation), dosing, monitoring (aPTT, ACT), clearance
LMWH: molecular differences, anti-Xa activity, dosing and renal considerations
Fondaparinux: synthetic pentasaccharide mechanism (AT-dependent factor Xa inhibition), dosing and limitations
Direct thrombin inhibitors (argatroban, bivalirudin): mechanism, metabolism and monitoring
Oral direct factor Xa inhibitors (DOACs, e.g., apixaban) overview
Adverse effects: bleeding risks, osteoporosis, hyperkalemia, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (overview)
Interactions with antithrombin and reversal/antidote considerations

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Cardiac Surgery and Cardiopulmonary Bypass: Hemostatic Considerations
chapters.description: How cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and cardiac surgery alter hemostasis, standard intraoperative anticoagulation strategies, and postoperative bleeding and thrombosis risks.
subtopics: Impact of CPB on platelets and coagulation (hemodilution, platelet dysfunction)
Rationale for high-dose UFH during CPB and monitoring with activated clotting time (ACT)
Protamine reversal of heparin and reperfusion effects
Postoperative inflammatory and acute phase responses affecting coagulation (fibrinogen elevation)
Perioperative strategies for thromboprophylaxis after cardiac surgery
Typical postoperative platelet count trajectories and expected nadirs
Transfusion thresholds and management in cardiac surgery

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT): Clinical Features and Epidemiology
chapters.description: Epidemiology, clinical presentation, risk factors, timing, and complications of classical (heparin-dependent) HIT.
subtopics: Incidence of HIT in different clinical settings (medical, surgical, cardiac surgery)
Typical timing of onset after heparin exposure (days 5–10) and rapid-onset variants
Clinical signs: thrombocytopenia patterns and thrombotic complications (venous and arterial)
4Ts scoring system and pretest probability assessment
Risk factors: type of heparin, duration, surgical procedures, prior heparin exposure
Natural history, morbidity and mortality associated with HIT

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Autoimmune Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (aHIT): Mechanisms and Clinical Spectrum
chapters.description: Pathophysiology, distinguishing features, and clinical implications of autoimmune HIT, in which antibodies can activate platelets independent of heparin.
subtopics: Definition and distinguishing laboratory/clinical features of aHIT vs typical HIT
Mechanisms of heparin-independent platelet activation by anti-PF4 antibodies
Clinical presentations: severity, prolonged thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy
Triggers and relation to recent heparin exposure
Implications for management and prognosis
Serological heterogeneity and variants with Fc receptor resistance

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Diagnostic Testing for HIT: Immunoassays and Functional Assays
chapters.description: Principles, performance characteristics and interpretation of laboratory tests used to diagnose HIT, including PF4/polyanion immunoassays and functional platelet activation assays like the serotonin-release assay (SRA).
subtopics: PF4/polyanion ELISA: antigen target, optical density (OD) interpretation, sensitivity and specificity
Rapid immunoassays (e.g., particle gel, lateral flow) and their performance
Functional assays: SRA, heparin-induced platelet activation (HIPA), flow cytometry-based activation tests
Typical SRA profiles: heparin-dependent activation at low heparin and inhibition at high heparin
Interpretation of heparin-independent activation and indeterminate results
Pre-analytical factors (platelet donor variability, sample handling, platelet clumping) affecting assays
Reporting, turnaround times and reflex algorithms

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Serological and Mechanistic Laboratory Concepts Specific to HIT Testing
chapters.description: Advanced laboratory concepts underpinning HIT testing, including role of platelet Fc receptor blockade, use of monoclonal antibodies (e.g., IV.3) in assays, and assay controls.
subtopics: FcγRIIa blockade (monoclonal antibody IV.3) rationale and interpretation
Heparin dose–response curves in SRA (0, low, high heparin concentrations)
Characterizing heparin-independent vs heparin-dependent antibodies
Platelet donor selection, platelet responsiveness and quality control
Use of serial testing to document evolving antibody profiles
Laboratory criteria for positive, negative and indeterminate SRA results

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Laboratory Evaluation and Interpretation of Thrombocytopenia and Consumptive Coagulopathy
chapters.description: How to interpret laboratory findings in thrombocytopenia with or without consumptive coagulopathy, including recognition of hemolysis, schistocytes, and acute phase reactants.
subtopics: Complete blood count and peripheral blood smear interpretation (platelet clumps, schistocytes)
Markers of hemolysis: haptoglobin, LDH, bilirubin, reticulocyte count
Coagulation studies: PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer in DIC and hypercoagulable states
Interpreting elevated fibrinogen as acute phase response vs consumption
Role of serial laboratory trends vs single measurements
Pre-analytical artefacts causing spurious thrombocytopenia

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Differential Diagnosis of Postoperative Thrombocytopenia
chapters.description: Comprehensive differential diagnosis for thrombocytopenia in the postoperative period, with distinguishing clinical and laboratory features.
subtopics: Expected postoperative platelet count nadir after major surgery
Sepsis-related thrombocytopenia and DIC
Transfusion-related causes: post-transfusion purpura, transfusion reactions
Thrombotic microangiopathies: TTP, HUS (clinical clues and lab differences)
Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia (timing, implicated drugs)
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia timing, risk and distinguishing features
Other causes: bone marrow suppression, hypersplenism, autoimmune thrombocytopenia

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Management Principles for HIT and aHIT
chapters.description: Guidelines and principles for managing suspected or confirmed HIT and autoimmune HIT, including immediate actions, anticoagulant alternatives, and duration of therapy.
subtopics: Initial steps when HIT suspected: stop all heparin exposures and heparin-containing devices
Choice of non-heparin anticoagulants (argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, DOACs)
Dosing, monitoring and adjustment of alternative anticoagulants
Role and rationale for intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in aHIT
When to start warfarin or DOACs and overlap considerations
Duration of anticoagulation after HIT with or without thrombosis
Management of bleeding risk and transfusion considerations during severe thrombocytopenia

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Pharmacology, Monitoring and Practical Use of Argatroban and Other Parenteral Agents
chapters.description: Detailed pharmacology, dosing strategies, monitoring, and complications of argatroban and other parenteral non-heparin anticoagulants used in HIT.
subtopics: Argatroban: mechanism (direct thrombin inhibitor), hepatic metabolism, dosing adjustments
Monitoring argatroban with aPTT and laboratory interactions (INR effects)
Bivalirudin: mechanism, renal considerations and use in PCI/cardiac surgery
Danaparoid and availability issues
Fondaparinux as off-label therapy for HIT: dosing, renal clearance, monitoring
Transitioning between parenteral agents and oral anticoagulants

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) in Immune-Mediated Thrombocytopenia
chapters.description: Mechanisms, indications, dosing considerations, expected responses, and limitations of IVIG when used to treat immune-mediated platelet disorders including aHIT.
subtopics: Mechanisms of action: Fc receptor blockade, anti-idiotype antibodies, modulation of complement and cytokines
Standard dosing regimens and repeat dosing rationale
Expected time-course of platelet response and markers of efficacy
Risks and adverse effects of high-dose IVIG (thrombotic risk, renal dysfunction)
Relative efficacy in ITP versus aHIT and factors predicting response
Interaction of IVIG with laboratory assays and interpretation

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Consumptive Coagulopathy, DIC and Thrombotic Microangiopathy
chapters.description: Pathophysiology and clinical-laboratory features of consumptive coagulopathy, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and thrombotic microangiopathies relevant to severe HIT presentations.
subtopics: Pathogenesis of DIC and laboratory diagnostic criteria
Distinguishing DIC from TTP/HUS: platelet count, schistocytes, ADAMTS13 testing
Laboratory patterns: fibrinogen consumption, rising D-dimer, prolonged PT/aPTT
Clinical consequences: bleeding vs thrombosis balance
Management principles for consumptive coagulopathy in the setting of thrombosis

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Stroke Pathophysiology, Ischemic Stroke Imaging and Antithrombotic Considerations
chapters.description: Mechanisms of ischemic stroke, principles of neuroimaging for diagnosis, and general considerations for anticoagulation in the context of acute cerebral ischemia and hemorrhagic risk.
subtopics: Ischemic stroke mechanisms: embolic vs thrombotic etiologies
Basic CT brain interpretation for acute infarction and hemorrhage
Timing and risks of anticoagulation after ischemic stroke
Anticoagulant selection and bleeding risk stratification in the peri-stroke period
Neurological assessment scales and monitoring for deterioration
Rehabilitation principles and prognosis indicators

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Antithrombin Physiology and Replacement Therapy
chapters.description: Role of antithrombin in coagulation, laboratory measurement, clinical consequences of deficiency, and rationale for antithrombin concentrate administration with certain anticoagulants.
subtopics: Antithrombin structure, synthesis and physiological function
Laboratory measurement and interpretation of antithrombin levels
Consequences of low antithrombin on anticoagulant efficacy (especially indirect agents)
Indications, dosing and monitoring of antithrombin concentrate
Interaction with fondaparinux and heparin efficacy

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Epidemiology, Risk Assessment and Clinical Decision Tools for HIT
chapters.description: Frameworks for assessing HIT probability, epidemiologic data guiding clinical decision-making, and use of clinical scoring systems integrated with laboratory testing.
subtopics: 4Ts score components and application (thrombocytopenia, timing, thrombosis, other causes)
Positive and negative predictive values of 4Ts combined with lab tests
Pretest probability stratification and test utilization strategies
Population-level incidence and risk modifiers for HIT
Algorithmic approaches to diagnosis and management endorsed by guidelines
Health system considerations: test availability, turnaround time and referral to specialized labs
